_README: The script for this app's store/social video. Read by the shared scripts in the `iboalali-apps`
kit. See the `store-video` skill for the full shape and for what each step verb does.
Two passes run over `scenes`: a rehearsal that resolves every tag to screen coordinates, then a
recorded pass that replays those coordinates on a freshly reset device. Both passes start from
the same state, which is why the coordinates stay valid.
THE SUBJECT OF THIS VIDEO CANNOT HAPPEN ON THE RECORDING DEVICE. The story is a root check that
SUCCEEDS, and no emulator is rooted: the AOSP `su` on a userdebug image refuses any caller that
is not shell or root, so `Shell.isAppGrantedRoot()` is false no matter what is installed. Even
sideloading the real Magisk app only reaches 'root available, not granted': the package probe
fires while the grant does not. So the result is armed from outside the app instead; see
_locales: English only for now, deliberately. The app ships five languages (en, de, es, ru, ar) and its
Play listing covers all five, so the other four are worth making, but the story and pacing get
approved once, in one language, before four more takes are shot against them.
Adding one is: a caption per scene plus an endCard.subtitle/cta.action here, a localeTags entry,
and one `video-record --locale <name>` run. Unlike Hide Persistent Notifications, it needs NO
rootable image and no reboot between languages. See setup.localeScope.

_note: Taken from the launcher icon, which is the app's only real brand mark: a white '#' on Material
Deep Purple 500 (#673AB7, `md_purple_500` in colors.xml, despite the name). The plate is that
purple taken most of the way to black so the phone stays the brightest thing in frame, and the
accent is the same hue lifted until dark text sits legibly on it.
Deliberately NOT the app's Material theme, whose burnt orange (#AB3500) never reaches the
screen: the app calls DynamicColors on API 31+, so what the camera sees is the device
wallpaper's palette, not the bundled one. Branding the plate off a palette the footage does not
contain would clash with the footage on every device it is recorded on.

_skin: A real SDK skin: the hardware image IS the frame, so the proportions are a real phone's. It
requires an AVD whose resolution matches the skin's display exactly. pixel_9_pro_xl is
1344x2992, so record on Pixel_9_Pro_XL (or the _root clone). The compositor checks and refuses
This app has a second reason to care which handset the frame draws, and it is unique among the
three: the main screen PRINTS THE DEVICE NAME. A Pixel 9 Pro XL body around a screen reading
'emulator / emu64xa' is the kind of detail that is invisible until someone sees it and then
_recordingDevice: The AVD's build properties are patched so the device card reads like the phone in the frame:
Out of the box an emulator reports model `sdk_gphone64_x86_64` and device `emu64xa`, which the
marketing-name lookup renders as 'emulator', and the app shows both on the main screen, directly
under the result. `ro.*` properties cannot be set at runtime even as root ('Failed to set
property'), and `-prop` on the emulator command line accepts only `qemu.*`, so this is an edit
emulator -avd Pixel_9_Pro_XL_root … -writable-system    # remount is refused without it
adb remount && adb reboot                               # overlayfs needs the reboot
vendor wins over system_ext in the default ro.product.property_source_order, so vendor is the
one that matters; system_ext is patched to match so the two cannot disagree later. Originals are
worth keeping: the change survives reboots and outlives whatever it was recorded for.

_package: The DEBUG applicationId, on purpose. Two things this video needs exist only in a debug build:
1. `DemoRootOverride`, the armed result. The FAB then runs the release path exactly (checking
snackbar, spinner, ~1s, result animation, success haptic) with only the answer decided in
advance. Without arming, a debug FAB opens the developer result PICKER, which would sit in
the middle of the shot; a release FAB runs a real check, which on this device answers 'not
2. Nothing else. The APK is otherwise the production one.
A debug build also carries three things the camera must NOT see: app_name 'Basic Root Checker
(Debug)', a blue launcher background and a blue splash icon, all of them in app/src/debug/res.
Build the take's APK with that folder moved aside, exactly as the screenshot export neutralises
versionNameSuffix '-debug' is left alone: it only shows on the About screen, which this journey
_clearForeignNotifiers: Needed even though this video never opens the shade, because two `android` notifications put
ICONS in the status bar that demo mode does not remove: a filled warning triangle and a
Safety-Center shield ('set a screen lock'). `notifications -e visible false` does not touch
them (they survive it) and `dumpsys statusbar` reports `mIcons=` empty, so they do not look
like notification icons either. Snoozing the notifications is what clears them.
Snoozing rather than dismissing is the only lever available for a notification we do not own,
and it lapses on its own long after the take. The recorder force-stops non-system posters and
_localeScope: Per-app locale (`cmd locale set-app-locales`), not the device's. Every frame of this video is
the app's own UI. There is no notification shade, no quick-settings tile, no permission
dialog, and the status bar is in demo mode showing a fixed clock and no text. So nothing on
screen is rendered by the framework, and there is nothing for the device language to change.
Which means the other four languages need no rootable image, no `setprop persist.sys.locale`
and no reboot between takes. Hide Persistent Notifications needs all three, because ITS subject
is a framework surface; this app should not inherit that cost.
The recorder applies it after the warm-up launch, on every pass: `pm clear` drops a per-app
locale, and one set before the package has ever run reports success and is silently gone by the
_emulatorDisplayOverride: null: record at the AVD's native 1344x2992, which is what the pixel_9_pro_xl skin expects.
Only reach for this if the emulator is rasterising in software, and check that first, because
software rendering is almost always a stale XAUTHORITY rather than an absent GPU:
adb shell dumpsys SurfaceFlinger | grep -iE '^GLES:'   # SwiftShader = software
The override costs inset correctness (the status-bar and cutout insets do not scale with
`wm size`) and with a working GPU buys nothing.
_pressOffsetMs: Carried over from the sibling app's measurement on the same AVD and the same capture path.
Re-measure if the press ring drifts off the finger: sample a frame at a logged press time, and
if the on-screen reaction has already begun, make this more negative.
It matters more here than it does there. This video has exactly ONE press in it, so there is no
second marker for the eye to average against. If it sits wrong, that is the whole video.
_tapDwell: beforeMs exceeds pressLeadMs plus the marker's fade, so the ring is sitting still on an
unchanged screen for about a quarter-second before the finger lands. Show the press, then press.
showTouches asks Android for its own touch circle, but that overlay layer is not captured by
screenrecord on an API 37 emulator, so it is off and the compositor draws the marker from the
press log instead; leaving both on would double the indicator.

_hideNotificationIcons: true here, unlike Hide Persistent Notifications, where the row of stuck icons IS the problem
being shown. Nothing in this story involves notifications, so any icon in the bar is a stray
from whatever the emulator last ran.

_absentKeys: No notificationListener, personaPackagePrefix, personas or clearForeignNotifiers: this app has
no notification listener and needs no staged clutter. They are optional in the recorder, which
they were not until this storyboard existed, since it had only ever driven one app.

_note: The extras arm the result before a single frame is recorded, so nothing in the journey has to
reach for it later. `monkey` cannot carry extras, so the recorder switches this step to an
explicit `am start` against the resolved launcher activity: same cold start, same splash.
3200ms because a cold start spends the first ~1.5s on the splash screen and the entrance
animation, leaving the viewer about 1.7s on the resting screen: enough to take in the empty
status card, its 'tap the # button' hint, and the device card underneath.
The single press in the video. tapDwell adds 750ms of settle before it and 300ms after, so
this scene is ~2.2s in total.
`check_fab` is a testTag added for this journey. Addressing the FAB by its content description
would have worked in English and broken in the other four languages. The rule is ids, never
text, and this is the control the whole video turns on.
The 900ms tail covers the checking state: the snackbar rising, the spinner replacing the
status glyph. The result lands about a second after the press, so the scene boundary falls
roughly where the answer appears.
Nothing happens here on purpose. The scene exists to hold on the payoff: the green check
scaling in, 'Your Device has Root access', 'via Magisk v29.0' underneath, and the device card
below it naming the same phone the frame is drawing.
The trailing wait is also what the end card fades in over. The compositor freezes the take's
LAST FRAME and cross-fades from it, so whatever the screen is doing when the recorder stops is
what the viewer stares at for three seconds. Everything has to be settled by then. Check it
after any change to this scene:
ffmpeg -sseof -0.3 -i raw.mp4 -frames:v 1 out.png

endCard.title: Basic Root Checker

subtitle.default: Is your device rooted? Find out instantly.

_cta: The short link, verified 200 and redirecting to the app's page. 16 characters, so the pill's
autosizing leaves it at full size. The printed string drops the scheme because 'https://' costs
eight characters of legibility and tells the viewer nothing; the QR's payload keeps it, because
a scheme-less payload is ambiguous and some readers surface it as plain text with nothing to
tap. The compositor compares the two and refuses to build if they disagree.
characters, unreadable at any size that fits, and absurd on the listing cut where the viewer is
The QR is not dead weight on the vertical cut even though you cannot scan a code with the phone
displaying it: Android's Circle to Search reads QR codes off the device's own screen, and the
audience for an Android root checker is exactly the people who have it.
Wording carries no price claim and no Google Play badge artwork, so the same card is safe in
feeds AND as the Play listing's video, whose guidance discourages both.

_audio: The same bed as Hide Persistent Notifications, deliberately: one track across the apps reads as
a house sound rather than as reuse, the way the plate, the bezel and the end-card layout already
do. CC0 is what makes that free: no attribution obligation to carry into every future re-post,
and no bookkeeping when a cut is re-published years later.
The file is COPIED into this repo rather than referenced across repos. 6.7MB duplicated is the
cheaper mistake: a relative path into a sibling checkout breaks on any machine that does not have
it, and the licence has to travel with the asset to be worth anything.
Licence rules, since this is where the next track gets chosen: NonCommercial disqualifies one
outright however good it sounds; these videos market an app. CC0 beats CC-BY. Free Music
Archive's own filters are not trustworthy on their own; open each candidate's page and confirm.
startAt 0 takes the track's opening. The source runs 4 minutes and this cut is 12.7 seconds, so
if the intro is too sparse to carry the video, move startAt to a more developed bar rather than
reaching for gainDb. The mastering targets -16 LUFS either way.
-16 LUFS, not the -14 platforms normalise to: this track measures -20.2 LUFS with only -2.0 dBTP
of headroom, so -14 needs gain the peaks cannot absorb and loudnorm abandons linear mode. Verify
the output stays below -1.0 dBTP; platforms only ever turn content down, so delivering slightly
quiet is safe and delivering something that clips is not.
